smoke_caveat: The AFTER chip's SCL band flags almost none of it as cloud (see masked_fraction_after), but a bright/low-saturation pixel heuristic on the true-colour chip (smoke_like_pixel_fraction_after) finds 20% of the chip looks like smoke or haze. Sen2Cor's SCL classifier is built to detect cloud, not smoke, and visibly misses the plumes visible in after.png. Part of the AFTER mean_ndvi drop may therefore be smoke attenuation rather than canopy loss; this could not be corrected for with the SCL band alone. The control chip shows no such contamination in either scene (smoke_like_pixel_fraction 0% / 0%).

control.rationale: Control at (-10.9, -54.15) is ~19.8 km SW of the target, read from the SAME two Sentinel-2 items as the target (before=S2C_MSIL2A_20250929T134721_R024_T21LZJ_20250929T184014, after=S2A_MSIL2A_20260827T135131_R024_T21LZJ_20260827T233711) so it shares season, sun angle, sensor and atmosphere. Selected before inspecting its NDVI: zero NASA FIRMS thermal detections within ~5.5km in the loaded alerts.json (394 detections total), and ESA WorldCover 2021 dominant class 'Tree cover' (100.0% tree-cover pixels in a ~1.1km box). Its own NDVI (0.544 before, 0.496 after) is reported as a post-hoc sanity check, not as the selection criterion: it is below the >0.7 closed-canopy rule of thumb, consistent with target NDVI in this same pair of scenes (0.475/0.408) also sitting well under 0.7 — this Amazon-Cerrado transition forest reads lower than humid rainforest on Sentinel-2 NDVI generally, not a sign the control is non-forest.

source: Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC API, collection sentinel-2-l2a, assets visual/B04/B08/SCL; control read from the identical before/after items as the target; ESA WorldCover 10m 2021 for land-cover cross-check; NASA FIRMS detections from data/alerts.json for control proximity check.
